correctness.rationale: The object is the first entrance time from the initial difference pair into the forward-invariant set of positive unequal odd pairs, not distance to a terminal cycle. The known exact one-step digit formulas imply only the interior mixed-parity line d+e=B needs two steps; diagonal states always need two; boundary e=0 has one unique three-step state. The complete disjoint partition gives N0,N1,N2,N3. For each pair, the exact word multiplicity follows from endpoint/interior middle digits and multinomial permutations, yielding W0,W1,W2,W3 through finite symbolic sums valid for every odd B>=5. Independent exact integer arithmetic recomputed state counts for every odd base 5..101 and direct word counts for bases 5,7,9,11. Asymptotics follow from polynomial leading terms. No finite experiment substitutes for the displayed general proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 full text proves a uniform 3-step entrance bound and a pointwise transition table but does not calculate the parity-sensitive entrance-depth frequencies or give the random-word distribution. The exact weighting of each difference state by its four-digit multiplicity requires an additional count. The examined 2021 full text concerns distance to a nonzero fixed point and fixed-point basin proportions, not first entry into the odd stable region for every odd base. The 2022 full text classifies cycles for general odd bases; it does not present the four-digit entrance distribution. No covering exact enumeration was found by actual textual and semantic searches; this is evidence of a gap, not a proof of worldwide uniqueness.

value.rationale: First-entry depth into the projective-doubling region is the canonical transient quantity underlying the 2026 bounded-preperiod theorem. A full two-ensemble enumeration answers how common the exceptional delays actually are; the exactly one worst-case difference state, explicit word count and 1/B versus 1/B² decay sharply quantify the contrast between worst-case and typical dynamics. The result is a natural all-odd-base exact invariant with a clear sampling interpretation, not an arbitrary finite computation. It does not purport to prove another terminal-cycle theorem; modest derivation-from-transition-map scope and access risks are disclosed.
